title: What the night may settle without the owner
rule: Most restrictive match wins (owner_only > night_proposes > night_decides). A change that matches nothing is night_proposes. A night_decides entry matches only when its proof attributes are present and true; a missing proof is no match. A standing prohibition is owner_only.

exam.note: night_decides takes effect only while this policy version has scored min_accuracy on at least min_items owner decisions made AFTER frozen_at (policy/exam-v2.json plus the plugin store, grown at night). Fewer items, or a lower score: every night_decides answer degrades to night_proposes (src/rooms/policy/exam.ts). policy/exam.json (32 items) is history: version 1 scored 14/32 = 0.438 on it, and every later version has seen it.

versions.exam: policy/exam-v2.json + plugin store policy:exam-v2 (decisions after the freeze)
versions.changes: standing_prohibitions concept (8 entries, each with its own source quote); rule_trial_apply moved from night_decides to night_proposes on design-side evidence d7, d10, d11 (against it: d9, d8 and the rollback a trial has; reasoning in docs/night-policy.md; not derived from the exam result); frozen_at/frozen_hash/min_items; exam grows at night

split.design_items: design_items below: the decisions this file was written from. Their ids start with d. since_version marks the ones added for a later version (absent = 1).
split.exam_items: policy/exam.json (v1, history): decisions version 1 was NOT written from. Ids x1... A test fails when an id sits on both sides or when an entry example cites an exam item. For version 2 and later the whole of exam v1 is in-sample: this file's standing prohibitions quote memory files that v1 exam items also cite (marked cited_by_v1_exam), and the miss analysis of v1 was read before version 2 was written.
split.live_items: policy/exam-v2.json + the plugin store (key policy:exam-v2): owner decisions with a decided_at after frozen_at, appended at night (src/rooms/policy/live-exam.ts). Ids y_<hash>. Only items decided after the version's frozen_at score it.
split.time_cut: v1: rule-proposal decisions up to 2026-10-14 are design (the five owner revocations of 2026-10-01/03); decisions from 2026-10-15 on are exam v1. Memory files: see design_items; every other memory file was exam v1. v2: anything decided after frozen_at is unseen; everything before is seen.

descriptor_vocabulary.note: Standing prohibitions match what the caller declares. A night-loop caller must put these kinds/attrs on a change that does the thing; a change that does not declare it is not recognised (it falls to the other lists or to night_proposes).

change_descriptor.note: What a caller hands to classifyChange. Every field is optional except that a descriptor with no kind, files, settings or tables is unknown (night_proposes).
change_descriptor.kind: string, what the change is, e.g. lp_fault_repair, docs_regenerate, rule_adopt, setting_change, data_delete
change_descriptor.files: string[], repository-relative paths the change touches
change_descriptor.settings: string[], setting keys the change writes
change_descriptor.tables: string[], database tables the change writes
change_descriptor.attrs: object of string|number|boolean proofs, e.g. bench_subset_passed, auto_revertible, always_on, irreversible

matcher.note: A matcher is an AND of the fields it carries; an entry matches when ANY of its matchers matches. Globs: * stays inside a path segment, ** crosses segments, ? is one character; matching is case-insensitive and paths are normalised (./ and .. are resolved, a path that leaves the repository starts with ../).
fields: files_any (some touched file matches some glob)
files_all (every touched file matches some glob; needs at least one file)

night_decides.description: Repair of a failure class that is Lane Pilot's own fault, accepted only with the bench subset passing and a one-step revert ready.
examples: close the class 'wildcard folder patterns own their contents' with a regression test
stop the relay retrying archived PM chats

night_decides.description: Regeneration of generated documentation pages; only when every touched file is a docs file.
examples: nightly docs pass rewrites docs/*.md and packages/*/docs/*.md

night_decides.description: A memory note (not the core) reaches its end of life and is retired.
examples: note past its expires_at is archived

night_decides.description: Retire a harness tree that lost against the incumbent on the bench.
examples: trial arm B lost by the alternation rule and is retired

night_decides.description: Deploy or release of a change whose full suite and post-deploy drill are green and that rolls back by itself.
examples: bb-plugin-push of a green tree, then gh release

night_proposes.description: Any rule goes into force, on trial or not. Version 1 let the night do this alone (a trial can be revoked). Version 2 proposes it: an accepted rule is core memory read by every writer (d10), core memory edits are proposals (memory_core_edit), the owner took back the first five trial rules himself (d7) and said rules must not pile up (d11). Revocability does not make the change his to skip.
examples: adoptRuleProposal puts a model-written rule on trial
the owner accepts a rule from the Rules tab

night_proposes.description: A rule that skips the relevance pick and rides in every prompt.
examples: a model-written rule marked always_on

night_proposes.description: Default model, provider, reasoning effort, service tier or agent for a role.
examples: writer default moves to another model
a role picker is reset to global

night_proposes.description: A stage is added to, removed from or reordered in the pipeline.
examples: add a code critic stage before acceptance

night_proposes.description: Any edit of the work graph: workflow definitions and the workflow engine.
examples: edit workflows/lp-task-pipeline.json

night_proposes.description: Change of the project's core memory (rules and conventions every agent reads).
examples: trim the core instead of failing

owner_only.description: Money, quotas and budgets: caps on attempts, tokens, wall time, children, daily judge calls, memory budgets.
examples: raise run.max_tokens
raise dailyJudgeCap

owner_only.description: Writing, moving or re-fencing secrets and the Env Catalog access model. Using a key as an agent is not a change and is not classified here.
examples: rewrite how env_get serves keys
touch .env files

owner_only.description: Anything on data that cannot be undone: deletes, drops, history rewrites, emptying trash.
examples: DELETE FROM a core table without a backup
git push --force
project_delete of a sandbox project

owner_only.description: The judge: acceptance and integration gates, drills, the canary and the full-suite gate, the code that decides done or not done.
examples: loosen the owns-paths gate
turn night_review.auto_merge on

owner_only.description: The fixed bench set the night is measured against.
examples: swap a task in the bench subset

owner_only.description: Verification thresholds: accuracy bars, acceptance scores, exam threshold.
examples: lower REVIEW_ACCURACY from 0.8

owner_only.description: This policy, its exam, its classifier and its tests.
examples: edit policy/night-policy.json
edit policy/exam.json

owner_only.description: Owner login, caller checks and confirmation forms: the owner rejected them (2026-10-08); only the owner brings one back.
examples: agent-caller refusal on plugin install

owner_only.description: A change outside this repository cannot be benched or reverted by the night.
examples: edit a sibling plugin repository
edit an absolute path

standing_prohibitions_note: Things the owner said must never be done. Each is owner_only, carries the words it comes from and the file/line, and may only grow (tests/policy/growth.test.ts). Sources are design-side material only: memory files and BB memory read as a whole, never an exam item. cited_by_v1_exam marks sources that v1 exam items also cite; those v1 items are in-sample for version 2. A change is recognised by the kinds/attrs it declares (descriptor_vocabulary).

standing_prohibitions.description: OpenCode v1 (acp-opencode) is removed from Lane Pilot; nothing brings it back.
examples: enable provider acp-opencode for a role
write a setting under providers.acp-opencode

source.quote: any new OpenCode code targets provider id `opencode2` and the v2 HTTP API/plugin SDK; never reintroduce acp-opencode paths.

standing_prohibitions.description: Jev routes only the subagents a lane session spawns, never the session's own turns or the owner's messages.
examples: route the owner's chat message through Jev before the model sees it

source.quote: Jev routes ONLY subagents a lane session spawns (Claude jev-router agent.spawn, Lane Stack 1.65.3) — never the session's own turns/owner messages

standing_prohibitions.description: Lane rules and hooks never touch sessions unrelated to Lane Pilot: a lane hook acts only behind a lane marker.
examples: add a machine-wide hook with no LANE_* marker gate

source.quote: owner: lane rules must never touch sessions unrelated to Lane Pilot.

standing_prohibitions.description: Claude is never in fast mode unless the owner turns it on in that chat; no default, role or spawn sets the fast service tier.
examples: set the project default service tier to fast
spawn a helper thread with serviceTier fast

source.quote: the owner wants Claude never in fast mode unless he turns it on in that chat

standing_prohibitions.description: No bb connect expose and no getbb.app links; machines talk over WireGuard and the owner gets links on bb.vechkasov.pro.
examples: share a dev server with bb connect expose

source.quote: never suggest `bb connect expose` or getbb links; to share a dev server between machines use the machine's VPN address

standing_prohibitions.description: Closing an access is never a flat ban or a bare «Refused»: every legitimate consumer keeps a working path and a refusal says what to ask the owner and how.
examples: ban agent reads of a secret with no grant path

source.quote: Every legitimate consumer keeps a working path (owner grant once, plugin-caller pass, read classification) — never a flat ban.

standing_prohibitions.description: Parallel agents and single tasks never run the full test suite; the coordinator runs it once per batch.
examples: a writer task whose check is the whole vitest suite
six subagents each running the full suite

source.quote: When several agents/writers work in parallel, none of them runs the full test suite.

standing_prohibitions.description: Env Catalog get/set stays open to agents: the guard, shim and OpenCode lists never block it.
examples: add bb env-catalog get to the shell guard's blocked commands

source.quote: don't block `bb env-catalog get/set` in the LP guard/shim/OpenCode lists.
